title: Semilinear compact-support exchange is site reindexing
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient conventions of [def-pur-conventions]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $g:Y'\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ be an isomorphism of underlying schemes, and form its Cartesian square with $f':X'\to Y'$ and $g':X'\xrightarrow{\sim}X$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. No $k$-linearity of $g,g'$ is required. Choose a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow j\overline X\xrightarrow pY)$ and its base change $c'=(j',p')$, with induced isomorphism $\bar g:\overline X'\xrightarrow{\sim}\overline X$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the domains of [def-exchange-projection], use its specified unit--square--counit exchange and canonical open comparison, over $S=Y$. Its map
$$\operatorname{Ex}_!^c:L g^*Rp_*j_!\longrightarrow Rp'_*j'_!L g'^*$$
is precisely the natural isomorphism
$$g^{-1}Rp_*j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp'_*\bar g^{-1}j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp'_*j'_!g'^{-1}$$
induced by the site reindexing equivalences of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]; completed pullback along these isomorphisms has the same identification. The first factor is the specified direct-image mate, not a separately chosen comparison. These maps respect identity and successive isomorphism base changes and vertical composition of the compactifiable maps, under the canonical direct-image, open-extension and compact-support composition comparisons. On finite constructible finite-Tor inputs they commute with derived quotient-coefficient extension; they also commute with integral reduction, rationalization and common-stage coefficient extension on the specified coefficient domains. The integral comparisons are formed on the actual strict reduction towers using [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map], before $R\lim$; the rational and algebraically closed comparisons are their scalar-localized/common-stage images. For maps and objects in the compactification-independent field-base domains of [fix-lem-exchanges], insert those canonical compactification comparisons in the displayed identity.
